It is assumed the man in the river was Roderick based both on the description and the fact that he was seen walking near the river. Police further found footprints that led from the shore to the open water. No foul play is suspected in this matter and it is assumed Roderick drowned.

Case reference: 2014006028.CaseDesc: On January 18th, 2013, the Teton family checked into the New Otani Inn, located in Yokohama, Japan. Henrik sought the assistance of police in Yokohama and the Canadian Embassy, to no avail. Shortly thereafter, Henrik attended 52 Division to report the incident and his subsequent attempt to locate his family. Toronto Police requested the assistance of Japanese police to confirm Chieko’s and Takaya’s well-being and Chieko’s intentions.  It was confirmed that both are in good health and that Chieko does not wish her whereabouts be disclosed.

Case reference: 2012020055.CaseDesc:
The body of an Asian male was discovered by cleaning staff at the Northbrook Inn in Grand Rapids, Manitoba.  The individual had checked in at 15:30h after arriving on the bus from Winnipeg.  At 18:00h cleaning staff entered the room to find the occupant deceased in a chair.
It was learned that the subject checked into the hotel under the name "CHERON, Deoung".  A small black bag containing herbal medication was located in the room, which after translation from Korean revealed the prescription was issued to "PARK, Seng Dae"(variation of spelling PARK, Sang Dae).  It should be noted that the bus ticket-stub was located with the deceased identified "DUNG" as the individual who purchased the ticket.
Numerous checks were made with variety of agencies in an attempt to determine the man's identity.  It is believed he may be of Korean or Chinese decent.

Case reference: 2014003748.CaseDesc: On September 29, 1996, the police were contacted by a friend who reported that three of his hunting partners, including Glen Mymryk, had been missing from a hunting trip. The three men left in a loaded boat and reached halfway to their destination when they decided the water conditions were too challenging and they turned around. The men were bailing, but the waves were too much for them to handle. The motor stalled and they capsized. Glen was last seen floating away soon after the boat capsized. The sole survivor was rescued seven hours after the incident, at which point it was ascertained that the other two men had drowned.

At approximately 6:00 p.m., Gabriel contacted his father via mobile phone to inform him that he was unable to tow the cabin back to shore due to the strong winds. An hour later, Gabriel contacted his father once more to request that he contact the emergency services, as he was unable to return to the dock and was being swept towards the open sea. Despite a thorough search, the whereabouts of Gabriel remain unknown.

Case reference: 2014003215.CaseDesc: On June 24, 1972, a group of seven people, including Hank Ethier, were fishing on the Burntwood River. They were however unable to get their boat started and as a result they began to drift backwards towards the rapids. This group called for help and the other boat went to their aid. Hank jumped from his boat and swam to the second one. Once they reached the disabled boat everyone was told to get in. Both boats encountered the rapids. It is assumed Hank drowned as a result of the mishap.

The pilot had declared that the engine had stalled and that he was trying to reach Reindeer Island. He then stated that he was going into the water. Two RCMP and an Air Search and Rescue Hercules aircrafts conducted an aerial search. It was not possible to search the lake by boat as there was too much ice on the lake. All three are presumed dead from drowning or the impact of the crash.
